findings.reason: the previous attempt at this section (`c-s4-deferred-measured`) met parity and failed on timing alone, so a measure with no wall-clock arm can reproduce that outcome and still read as green.
findings.text: s4's four cases can all pass while a launch stays as slow as the 1,250–2,980 s `launch_seconds` the unit cites: case 1 counts calls to `review_coverage` and case 4 times a stubbed launcher, so nothing measures a real launch-decision cost; the earlier form of this unit carried a fleet-node timing arm ("the after figure is under five seconds"), and that arm has been removed

findings.reason: the node can satisfy case 1 and leave the per-request plan parse that dominates the pass in place, which is what case 1 is offered as evidence against.
findings.text: the memo is scoped to `review_coverage`, but every request in the same pass still pays the reads around it: `_plan_review_owed` calls `plan_review._section_digests(path)` at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3319`, `plan_html.read_state_file(path)` at 3328 and the document-contract walk at 3329–3337 per request, so "computed once per plan per pass" holds for one function and not for the pass's cost

findings.reason: an arm no implementation can fail spends a case on nothing and cannot distinguish a memo that invalidates correctly from one that never had a chance to be stale.
findings.text: s4's second case ("a stored review record added between two passes is seen by the second pass's decisions") is satisfied by the base revision, which has no memo and therefore always reads the store again; no negative control names it, so it is an arm that cannot fail

findings.reason: a coordinator running `--run` to launch one named request would get unrelated landings and releases, which is a behaviour the section's own `--once` complaint is about and which its measure cannot catch.
findings.text: s21 requires `crew admit --run` to run "for that one request only", but the only entry point it can reuse, `admit_until_stopped(once=True)` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:4386–4404`), also runs `_release_tick()` and starts a `_LandingWorker`; none of the three cases observes a release or a landing, so a `--run` that also releases waiters and lands deliveries satisfies every case
